A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WOMD-Reasoning and Motion-LLaVA. Their complete main texts, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original human evaluations, model benchmarks, numerical question-answering accuracy and ablation results.

after.justification: v3 retains original model evaluations and reports an expanded human assessment, additional baselines, data-scaling results and trajectory-prediction experiments.

M1.justification: Section 6.1 adds a language-assisted trajectory predictor: Motion-LLaVA interaction answers pass through T5 and MLP layers, then enter MultiPath++ through agent-specific cross-attention between its history and MCG encoders. This is a substantive new procedure. The original dataset-generation and Motion-LLaVA pipelines remain unchanged; agent-ID handling is newly documented.

E1.justification: v3 adds explicit downstream evaluation of language-assisted vehicle trajectory prediction on WOMD. v2 used motion prediction for encoder pretraining but evaluated the final systems through language answers. The underlying WOMD coverage and Q&A categories remain unchanged; additional datasets in Table 1 are literature comparisons, not newly used benchmarks.

E2.justification: Appendix A.7/Table 13 adds unfine-tuned LLaMA-Adapter v2.1, ViTA-1.5 and Qwen2.5-VL, plus fine-tuned LLaMA-Adapter v2.1. It does not report fine-tuned ViTA or Qwen results. Table 6 newly evaluates unaugmented MultiPath++ against its language-assisted counterpart. Existing LLaVA comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The reported human evaluation expands from three reviewers assessing 501 Q&As from 11 consecutive scenes to four reviewers assessing 1,610 Q&As. New experiments introduce trajectory evaluation using minFDE6 and MR6 and training-data scaling at 0.5M, 1M and full size. These extend the evaluation design without establishing changes to the retained benchmark settings.

E4.justification: Appendix A.11/Table 17 adds a focused sensitivity study testing how dataset size affects factual versus interaction-reasoning answers. Figures 5–6 also revise and expand the qualitative cases. The existing CoT, encoder-pretraining and fine-tuning-strategy ablations remain unchanged, relocated to Appendix A.10.

E5.justification: v2 Table 3 reports standard errors for human-evaluated category accuracies, including 3.51% for interactions and 10.00% for intentions. v3 replaces these with point accuracies without uncertainty estimates. The new model experiments introduce no repeated-run, confidence-interval or significance-test reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds trajectory results: Table 6 reports minFDE6 of 1.27 versus 1.18 and MR6 of 12.59 versus 11.69 for MultiPath++ without versus with language. Tables 13 and 17 add baseline and scaling scores. Human-evaluation results are replaced under the enlarged study, preventing direct accuracy comparisons. The original benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The new architecture description and empirical metric names introduce no substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The largest-dataset and interaction-reasoning contributions remain. However, v3's abstract, contribution statements and conclusion explicitly claim interaction prediction and traffic-rule-compliant planning capabilities, strengthening the application claim beyond v2's emphasis on accurate Q&A and potential downstream uses.

C2.justification: v3 removes v2's concluding discussion of limited human verification, inherited WOMD accuracy limitations and the simulation-to-real visual gap, although ongoing cleaning and missing camera data remain mentioned elsewhere. It adds interpretations of intention summaries as compliant planning, scaling trends as hierarchical learning, and language conditioning as improving prediction explainability. These materially revise the paper's interpretations and qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly documents agent-ID ranges, remapping and the per-agent motion prompt. Appendix A.4 supplies the downstream T5-v1_1-xxl encoder, batch size 128, learning rate 1e-4 and missing-caption fallback. Conversely, v3 omits v2's disclosure that numerical factual-answer evaluation used 130 questions. These are documentation changes, not evidence that retained experiments changed.

R1.justification: Table 1 expands the existing comparison with Rank2Tell, NuInstruct, nuCaption and Tod3Cap, explicitly recognizing another dataset covering all three interaction types. References also expand for the new baselines, T5 and newer driving work. The central positioning around large-scale, traffic-rule-aware language data remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially reframed around dataset applications. Model setup and metrics move into Methods, dataset discussion is reorganized, applications receive separate subsections, and main-text ablations move into an expanded appendix. This is extensive narrative and structural revision beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adopts ICML formatting and a single-column appendix, broadly rearranges displays, expands Table 1 and redesigns the human-evaluation table. v2 Figure 6 becomes two expanded interaction/planning figures, while new trajectory, baseline and scaling tables are added. Existing ablation tables are relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: The trajectory-prediction experiment supplies downstream evidence absent from v2's Q&A-focused evaluation; additional baselines, scaling analysis and the larger human assessment strengthen validation. However, removing uncertainty estimates and substantive limitations weakens transparency, while planning remains demonstrated through qualitative answers. The added evidence provides a useful but limited net improvement.
